design.seam: ProxyOrchestrator.init: the privilegeClient: PrivilegeClient? parameter is replaced, at the same position, by relayCommand: (@Sendable (PrivilegedBatchStep) async throws -> Void)? = nil, in the connectivityProbe style. The orchestrator's privilege client was used only by the relay. Nil (pm-proxy, which never passed a client, and agent runs) keeps the unchanged 'TCP relay unavailable: no privileged helper configured.' info path; nothing is sent.
design.composition: RuntimeHost.init builds its PlatformWork (same label io.github.srps.Conduit.daemon.platform-work) as a local before the orchestrator and assigns the existing platformWork property, now an init-assigned let. The closure is platformWork.run { Result { try auditedPrivilegeClient.execute(step.operation, values: step.values) } }.get(): the same audited client and the same execute(_:values:) call as before, so auth.privilege_request audit events are unchanged, on the same FIFO as the lifecycle surface blocks. Kernel imports unchanged.
design.async_relay: startTCPRelay/stopTCPRelay are async. Each advances tcpRelayGeneration in its deciding turn, before the command is sent, and applies tcpRelayActive and its log line on completion. Log text and levels unchanged; stop still clears the flag only on success.
design.lifecycle_callers: startTransparentProxy (three sites) and stopTransparentProxy await them. Both run only inside dnsLifecycle effects (runDNSStart, closeDNSListeners from stopDNS/restartDNS), so PhysicalLifecycle orders the relay commands, not when they were queued.
design.reassert: The tick (and each test entry point) takes a RelayReassertFence in its own turn: the relay generation and the DNS epoch. It begins only while dnsLifecycle.admitsRunning and no reassert is in flight. The probe runs outside the slot as before (utility queue for the tick/off-main path, inline for the test entry), so a slow connect never holds a stop's teardown. The reissue then runs as runInfallibleEffect(dnsLifecycle, epoch: fence.epoch). Inside it the generation is checked again: a restart keeps its epoch but its teardown moves the generation. A false from the slot, or a moved generation, emits the existing tcp_relay.reassert_superseded with the unchanged detail (host=, target=, relay_active=). tcp_relay.reasserted and tcp_relay.unresponsive are unchanged.
design.one_in_flight: transparentRelayReassertInFlight: set when a reassert begins, cleared when its task or entry point ends. A tick taken meanwhile begins nothing (beginTransparentRelayReassert returns nil), so the slot holds at most one reassert waiting beside the lifecycle effects. Each command stays bounded by the existing helper transaction budget; the AppleScript fallback refuses relay commands, so no authentication prompt starts.
design.test_entry_points: reassertTransparentRelay(), reassertTransparentRelay(host:targetPort:) (inline probe, test-only) and reassertTransparentRelayOffMain(host:targetPort:) are async; beginTransparentRelayReassert returns Task<Void, Never>?. Names and package access unchanged.

risks_and_remaining: Relay commands now wait behind any queued PlatformWork (accepted consequence): a transparent-proxy bind can start later than before. Nothing on a PlatformWork block waits on the orchestrator, so no deadlock.

No blind relay stop at quit, as in the base (the old AppState termination path that issued it was already gone): a relay a crashed earlier run left in the helper is not stopped by a quit; TCPRelayPlan replaces it at the next DNS start.

A reassert never begins while the DNS module's latest operation is a stop (dnsLifecycle.admitsRunning false). The timer only runs while a transparent proxy is published, so this changes nothing in production.

The two slot witnesses (kernel test and pm-sim row) give a beside-the-slot teardown up to 500 ms to show before asserting it did not run. That is a bounded negative check: on the correct code it costs that wait. The decisive assertion, the final relay state, is deterministic.
HeldCall .recorded leaves a released semaphore permit when the call was let through; no witness re-arms afterwards. The full actor-aware HeldCall generalization is still later work.
Phase 2 (actor retag) and diagnostics (1d) are untouched.
